deciding_assertions: test_inference.py imports is_array_like_deprecate_non_pandas from pandas.core.dtypes.common (all 799 tests of the module are missing before the fix); test_is_array_like_deprecate_non_pandas: duck array warns Pandas4Warning with match 'no longer be treated as array-like'
reason: The issue asks to deprecate is_array_like and to replace its internal uses with isinstance checks. It never names the helper is_array_like_deprecate_non_pandas, so a fix that deprecates is_array_like directly leaves the import failing and the whole test module fails to load. The warning text 'no longer be treated as array-like' is also not given by the issue.

deciding_assertions: test_embedded_nul_is_not_a_numeric_or_boolean_literal and test_embedded_nul_in_later_row with 1.5\x00xyz, 1e3\x00xyz, inf\x00xyz, -Infinity\x00x expect the field kept as a string; test_embedded_nul_is_not_a_float expects to_numeric to raise; test_error, test_scalar_fail, test_really_large_in_arr, test_xml_dtypes::test_wrong_dtype expect the message quote changed to 'Unable to parse string 'apple''
reason: The issue says the float path is not affected and that '1.5\x00xyz' reads as 1.5 on both engines, so there is nothing to fix there. The narrowest reasonable fix (length checks in str_to_int64/str_to_uint64, to_boolean and _bool_numeric_literal) passes the int and bool tests but fails every float test and the to_numeric tests. The changed error-message quote style is not in the issue either.

deciding_assertions: test_ambiguous_archive_closes_fsspec_handle: read_csv('memory://archive.zip') raises 'Multiple files found' and the fsspec OpenFile must be closed (opened[0].fobjects == []); test_ambiguous_archive_closes_handle[.zip/.tar]: the one _BytesZipFile/_BytesTarFile wrapper must be closed
reason: The issue reports a local zip path left open after the multiple-files error. A reasonable fix that closes the archive handles created in get_handle (or closes the wrapper before the raise) passes the zip and tar tests. It does not close the source stream that _get_filepath_or_buffer opened for an fsspec URL, a case the issue does not mention, so the fsspec test fails.

deciding_assertions: test_api_typing: allowed_typing lists RollingGroupBy, ExpandingGroupBy, ExponentialMovingWindowGroupBy, DatetimeIndexResamplerGroupBy, PeriodIndexResamplerGroupBy, TimedeltaIndexResamplerGroupBy; test_api_typing_deprecated_groupby_spelling[...] and _import: old names warn Pandas4Warning with match 'pandas.api.typing.{old} is deprecated' and return the new class
reason: The issue is only a question about why the capitalization differs; it asks for no change and proposes no fix. The tests need one specific design (rename six classes, including resampler classes the issue does not name, and keep the old names as deprecated aliases with an exact message). A fix that only answers the question, or renames without aliases, fails these tests.

deciding_assertions: test_negative_min_count_deprecated (reductions, groupby, resample), test_negative_min_count_deprecated_array, test_negative_min_count_deprecated_timedelta_index: min_count=-1 must emit Pandas4Warning matching "Passing a negative value for 'min_count' is deprecated" and return the same result as min_count=0
reason: The issue asks to raise a ValueError when min_count < 0. The tests expect a deprecation warning with an exact message and an unchanged result. The fix the issue asks for (raise ValueError) fails every fail-to-pass test.

deciding_assertions: test_replace_hits_nat_sentinel: match 'Out of bounds nanosecond timestamp: 1677-09-21 00:12:43.145224192'; test_constructor_*_nat_sentinel, test_to_datetime_hits_nat_sentinel (9 parser routes), test_to_datetime_nat_sentinel_message, test_parse_dates_c_fastpath_nat_sentinel* (read_csv C fast path falls back to strings or shifts into range)
reason: The issue asks only that Timestamp.replace(nanosecond=192) raise OutOfBoundsDatetime like nanosecond=191, whose message is 'Out of bounds timestamp: ... 00:12:43 with frequency ns'; the narrowest fix (raise that existing message when replace lands on iNaT) fails the regex that needs the word 'nanosecond' and the sub-second digits. The tests also require the same guard in the constructor (which the issue leaves to a separate fix), every to_datetime parser leg and the read_csv C fast path, which a fix of replace does not cover.

deciding_assertions: test_select_missing_raises: KeyError match "\['nope'\] not in index"; test_select_expression_* and test_select_kwargs_* (pd.col expressions, keyword computed columns, callables, alignment); test_select_set_raises / test_select_list_mixed_with_args_raises / test_select_expression_multiindex_*_raises: TypeError with exact messages; test_select_multiindex_mixed_depth*
reason: The issue is a draft that proposes a ValueError for a missing column and leaves wildcards and MultiIndex open; the test expects KeyError instead. Most tests check expressions, keyword computed columns, callables and MultiIndex mixed-depth rules that the issue does not ask for, plus new TypeError messages. A fix of the stated basic case (select labels by *args or a list, ValueError on missing) fails many of them.

deciding_assertions: test_add_offset_raises[all offset types]: off + BMonthEnd() raises TypeError matching 'unsupported operand type|Cannot add'; test_add_timedelta_to_anchored_offset_raises: MonthEnd/YearEnd/DateOffset(months=1) + timedelta raises 'unsupported operand type'; test_td64arr_addsub_anchored_offset_arraylike: message changed to 'unsupported operand type'
reason: The issue asks that DateOffset(days=1) + DateOffset(days=1) work like Day + Day. The tests instead keep offset composition unsupported and only check that the error is a normal 'unsupported operand type' TypeError for many offset types. The narrowest reasonable fix (add same-type offsets by summing n, leave other paths as they are) still raises the old 'has incorrect type' message for off + BMonthEnd() and fails every deciding assertion.

deciding_assertions: test_index_repr_float_nan[float32,float64,object]: idx._summary() == 'Index: 2 entries, 1.5 to NaN'; test_index_repr_complex_nan[complex64,complex128]: repr == "Index([(1+2j), (NaN-1j), (1+NaNj)], dtype=...)"
reason: The issue asks that Index repr show float NaN as 'NaN'. The narrowest reasonable fix (format a float NaN element as 'NaN' in the Index formatter) passes the repr checks for float and object dtypes, but fails the _summary assertion (the info summary line builds head and tail with an f-string, not the repr formatter) and the complex test, which needs a specific in-string replacement for a dtype the issue does not name; a fix that renders any NA element as 'NaN' gives 'NaN' for the whole complex value and also fails.

deciding_assertions: test_dtypes_basic.py module import: from pandas.io.parsers.base_parser import wrap_object_columns (all 1114 fail-to-pass tests are missing before the fix); test_wrap_object_columns_only_wraps_object: wrap_object_columns(col_dict, dtype, index) returns the int array unchanged and wraps only object columns
reason: The issue is a refactor that asks for a shared ParserBase method to build the DataFrame for the C and Python engines, without naming any function. The test file imports a new module-level helper wrap_object_columns with a fixed signature and behaviour; any refactor that does not add this exact name fails to import, so every fail-to-pass test fails.

deciding_assertions: test_invalid_date_kwarg_with_value_input / test_invalid_year_kwarg_with_value_input: ValueError match 'Cannot pass both a value to convert and date attributes'; test_invalid_date_kwarg_names_the_offending_arguments, test_tz_passed_positionally, test_components_without_year_report_value_form: exact text "..., got ['hour', 'minute']; 'tz' is keyword-only"; test_constructor_positional_keyword_gap_raises(_at_day), test_constructor_positional_explicit_none_gap_raises: 'Cannot leave a gap in the positional date attributes'; test_constructor_positional_tzinfo_slot*, test_datetime_reconstruction_keeps_tzinfo: 8th positional arg attached as tzinfo; test_read_pickle_legacy_timestamp_keeps_tz; test_timestamp_constructor_na_value_with_components: NaT input with components gives NaT
reason: The issue asks for an error (or possibly a deprecation warning) when a datetime value is mixed with component arguments, but gives no error class choice and no message. The narrowest reasonable fix raises an error with its own wording for datetime/Timestamp input plus components; it fails the exact new messages, and the tests also cover cases the issue never states (positional gaps with keywords, the tzinfo positional slot, legacy pickle loading via read_pickle, NaT input with components).

deciding_assertions: test_arrow.py test_str_replace_re_fallback: ArrowDtype str.replace with compiled pat, callable repl, case=False, flags=IGNORECASE, '\g<mid>' repl give results instead of NotImplementedError; test_str_extract_flags: extract with flags=re.IGNORECASE; test_str_count_flags: count with flags=re.ASCII; test_str_contains_match_compiled_pattern; test_str_match_multiline_flag; test_match_arrow_dtype_flags: match with re.MULTILINE and fullmatch with IGNORECASE on bool[pyarrow]
reason: The issue asks only that str.match with flags=re.ASCII works. The new test of exactly that case on the normal string dtypes (test_ascii_flag_applied) is not in fail_to_pass, so it already passes; all failing tests are for pd.ArrowDtype(pa.string()) and cover replace, extract, count, MULTILINE and compiled IGNORECASE patterns. A reasonable fix that makes ASCII mode work in str.match (even on ArrowDtype) fails the replace, extract and count tests.

deciding_assertions: All fail-to-pass tests (frame and series test_filter.py) call filter with a new cond= keyword or a positional mask/callable/pd.col expression and a new na= keyword ('raise', True, False), and check new messages such as 'Must pass a positional argument or one of `items`, `cond`', 'A list-like of booleans passed positionally to DataFrame.filter', 'cond passed to DataFrame.filter must be a one-dimensional boolean mask'
reason: The issue proposes a level argument for DataFrame.filter to select on one MultiIndex level. No test uses level; the tests check a boolean-mask cond parameter and an na parameter that the issue never names, with new messages. The narrowest reasonable fix (add level to filter) passes none of the fail-to-pass tests.

deciding_assertions: test_to_string_na_rep_none_and_na and test_to_html_na_rep_none_and_na [values5-object] ([1, None]) and [values7-object] ([1, pd.NaT]): 'None' not in result and count('foo') == 1; test_to_string_na_rep_explicit_nan: to_string(na_rep='NaN') on [None, NA, NaT, nan] object counts 'NaN' == 4 while to_string() shows each as itself, and a datetime Series with na_rep='NaN' shows 'NaN' instead of 'NaT'
reason: The issue asks that pd.NA be replaced by na_rep in to_string and to_xml. The narrowest reasonable fix makes an explicit na_rep apply to pd.NA (and fixes the to_xml fillna cast), keeping the existing deliberate output of None and NaT in object columns, and may detect the default by na_rep == 'NaN' as the datetime path already does. That fix passes the masked/arrow dtype cases but fails the object None and NaT cases and the explicit-'NaN' test, which change existing behaviour the issue does not mention.

deciding_assertions: test_complex_ordering_cmp_deprecated (arithmetic, masked, sparse) and test_real_cmp_complex_deprecated: tm.assert_produces_warning(Pandas4Warning, match='deprecated on complex data') for <, <=, >, >= and result still returned; test_numpy _compare_other expects the warning; test_clip_complex_deprecated / test_clip_complex_bound_deprecated: clip on complex data or with a complex bound warns
reason: The issue expects a TypeError like Python's for ordering comparisons of complex numbers. The tests instead expect a Pandas4Warning deprecation with the message 'deprecated on complex data' and a normal result, and also cover clip and real data compared against complex values. The narrowest reasonable fix (raise TypeError for <, <=, >, >= on complex data) fails every deciding assertion.

deciding_assertions: test_inference.py imports is_array_like_deprecate_non_pandas from pandas.core.dtypes.common (all 799 fail_to_pass tests are missing before the fix, so the import decides the whole file); test_is_array_like_deprecate_non_pandas: duck-typed array-like warns Pandas4Warning with match 'no longer be treated as array-like', pandas objects give no warning
reason: The issue asks to deprecate is_array_like and replace its internal uses with isinstance checks. The tests need a new helper name that the issue never gives, plus a new warning text, and they check a deprecation of duck-typed inputs at internal call sites rather than of is_array_like itself. The narrowest reasonable fix (warn in is_array_like, replace internal uses) fails the import and so every test in the file.

deciding_assertions: test_embedded_nul_is_not_a_numeric_or_boolean_literal and test_embedded_nul_in_later_row with float fields ('1.5 NUL xyz', '1e3 NUL xyz', 'inf NUL xyz', '-Infinity NUL x'): result['a'][0] == field; test_to_numeric::test_embedded_nul_is_not_a_float: to_numeric raises; test_error, test_scalar_fail, test_really_large_in_arr, test_bool_handling, test_xml_dtypes::test_wrong_dtype: message changed to single quotes "Unable to parse string 'apple' ..."; test_error_names_the_value_exactly; test_embedded_nul_is_not_a_python_int
reason: The issue asks to fix only the int64/uint64 and boolean converters and says the float path is not affected and needs no fix. A fix scoped to the issue keeps '1.5 NUL xyz' as 1.5, so the float cases and the to_numeric tests fail. The tests also need a changed quote style in the existing to_numeric error message and a fix of the Python-int fallback, which the issue does not name.

deciding_assertions: test_ambiguous_archive_closes_fsspec_handle: read_csv('memory://archive.zip') raises, then the fsspec OpenFile has fobjects == [] (OpenFile.close() must be called); test_ambiguous_archive_closes_handle[.tar]: the _BytesTarFile wrapper is closed
reason: The issue reports that a local zip archive stays open after the 'Multiple files' error. The narrowest reasonable fix closes the handles that get_handle opened (the _BytesZipFile, and the list of handles in general) when it raises. That fix passes the zip test and the tar test, but fails the fsspec test, which needs the remote source and its OpenFile (ioargs.close_handles) closed too. The issue does not mention that source.

deciding_assertions: test_api_typing: allowed_typing lists the *GroupBy spellings (DatetimeIndexResamplerGroupBy, ExpandingGroupBy, ExponentialMovingWindowGroupBy, PeriodIndexResamplerGroupBy, RollingGroupBy, TimedeltaIndexResamplerGroupBy) and not the old ones; test_api_typing_deprecated_groupby_spelling and _import: getattr of the old name warns Pandas4Warning with match 'pandas.api.typing.<old> is deprecated' and returns the new class
reason: The issue only asks why the capitalization differs; it proposes no change. The tests need one design among several options: rename six classes in pandas.api.typing (four of them are not named in the issue), hide the old names from the module listing, and keep them as aliases that emit Pandas4Warning with a given message. An answer, a plain rename, or plain aliases all fail.

deciding_assertions: All test_negative_min_count_deprecated tests (reductions, arrays, TimedeltaIndex, groupby, resample): min_count=-1 emits Pandas4Warning with match "Passing a negative value for 'min_count' is deprecated" and returns the min_count=0 result
reason: The issue asks to raise ValueError when min_count < 0. The tests expect a deprecation warning with an exact message that the issue does not give, and a result equal to min_count=0. They also cover groupby first/last/min/max, resample and array types that the issue does not name. The fix that the issue proposes (raise ValueError in sum and prod) fails every fail_to_pass test.

deciding_assertions: test_to_datetime_hits_nat_sentinel (9 parser routes), test_parse_dates_c_fastpath_nat_sentinel* (read_csv C fastpath), test_constructor_*_nat_sentinel and test_constructor_aware_datetime_offset_overflow (Timestamp constructor, tz shifts, OverflowError to OutOfBoundsDatetime); test_replace_hits_nat_sentinel and test_to_datetime_nat_sentinel_message: match 'Out of bounds nanosecond timestamp: 1677-09-21 00:12:43.145224192'
reason: The issue asks only that Timestamp.replace(nanosecond=192) raise OutOfBoundsDatetime like nanosecond=191, and says the constructor case is a separate fix. The narrowest reasonable fix (check for iNaT after the value is computed in replace and raise like the 191 path) fails all constructor, to_datetime and read_csv tests, and it also fails the replace test, because the 191 message shown in the issue is 'Out of bounds timestamp: 1677-09-21 00:12:43 with frequency 'ns'' while the test needs a new message with the sub-second digits.

deciding_assertions: test_select_missing_raises: KeyError "['nope'] not in index"; test_select_expression*, test_select_kwargs*: pd.col expressions and keyword arguments as in assign; test_select_multiindex_mixed_depth*; test_select_set_raises / test_select_list_mixed_with_args_raises / test_select_expression_*_raises: exact TypeError messages
reason: The issue drafts select(*labels) or select(list), assumes a ValueError for a missing column, and leaves wildcards and MultiIndex open. The narrowest reasonable fix (labels or one list, ValueError for missing labels) fails the KeyError test, every expression and keyword test, which the issue does not mention, and the TypeError tests whose messages the issue does not give.

deciding_assertions: test_add_offset_raises[all 24 offset types]: off + BMonthEnd() raises TypeError matching 'unsupported operand type|Cannot add'; test_add_timedelta_to_anchored_offset_raises: MonthEnd/YearEnd/DateOffset(months=1) + timedelta raises 'unsupported operand type'; test_td64arr_addsub_anchored_offset_arraylike: message 'unsupported operand type'
reason: The issue asks that DateOffset(days=1) + DateOffset(days=1) work and give a sum, like Day + Day. The tests instead expect offset + offset to keep raising, only with the standard Python TypeError message, for all offset types and for timedelta operands. A reasonable fix that makes DateOffset addition combine leaves the old 'has incorrect type' message for other types and fails every fail-to-pass test.

deciding_assertions: test_index_repr_complex_nan: repr gives '(NaN-1j)' and '(1+NaNj)' for complex values with a NaN part; test_index_repr_float_nan: idx._summary() == 'Index: 2 entries, 1.5 to NaN'
reason: The issue asks that a float NaN in an Index repr show as 'NaN' like Series/DataFrame. The narrowest reasonable fix (formatter returns 'NaN' for float NaN, also in object Index) passes the repr and bool/object assertions, but fails the _summary assertion (a different rendering, used by info(), that the issue does not name) and the complex test; an isna-based fix gives 'NaN' for the whole complex value, and only a text replace inside complex output gives the asserted '(NaN-1j)'.

deciding_assertions: test_dtypes_basic.py imports wrap_object_columns from pandas.io.parsers.base_parser; all 1114 fail-to-pass tests are missing before the fix because the module does not load; test_wrap_object_columns_only_wraps_object calls it with (col_dict, dtype, index)
reason: The issue asks for a refactor: one ParserBase method that builds the DataFrame for the C and Python engines. A reasonable refactor with any method name passes nothing, because the whole test module imports the new module-level helper wrap_object_columns, which the real fix adds and the issue never names.

deciding_assertions: test_invalid_date_kwarg_with_value_input / test_invalid_year_kwarg_with_value_input: ValueError match 'Cannot pass both a value to convert and date attributes'; test_invalid_date_kwarg_names_the_offending_arguments, test_tz_passed_positionally, test_components_without_year_report_value_form: exact text "..., got ['hour', 'minute']; 'tz' is keyword-only"; test_constructor_positional_keyword_gap_raises*/explicit_none_gap_raises: 'Cannot leave a gap in the positional date attributes'; test_constructor_positional_tzinfo_slot*: 8th positional arg attached as tzinfo; test_read_pickle_legacy_timestamp_keeps_tz: read_pickle of legacy (value, freq, tz) pickles; test_timestamp_constructor_na_value_with_components: Timestamp(None, year=2020) is NaT
reason: The issue asks that mixing a datetime input with by-component arguments raise some exception (or warn during a deprecation period) and gives no message. The narrowest reasonable fix raises ValueError with its own wording when ts_input is given together with year..microsecond; it fails every match= on the new message text, and it does not cover the positional-gap checks, the 8th positional tzinfo slot, the legacy pickle path, or the NaT-with-components cases, none of which the issue names. A fix that chooses the warning option the issue offers also fails.

deciding_assertions: All 15 fail-to-pass tests use ArrowDtype(pa.string()): test_str_count_flags (count with re.ASCII), test_str_contains_match_flags[contains/match/fullmatch], test_str_contains_match_compiled_pattern (IGNORECASE compiled pattern), test_str_match_multiline_flag (fullmatch with MULTILINE), test_str_replace_re_fallback (compiled pat, callable repl, case=False, flags, named-group repl), test_str_extract_flags (IGNORECASE), test_match_arrow_dtype_flags (MULTILINE, IGNORECASE). The new test_ascii_flag_applied (issue case on all standard string dtypes) is not in fail_to_pass.
reason: The issue asks only that str.match accept flags=re.ASCII. The new test of exactly that case on the standard string dtypes is not fail-to-pass, so it already passes before the fix; the failing tests are all for ArrowDtype strings, which the issue does not name. A reasonable fix that makes match (and its close siblings) honor re.ASCII does not make str.count, str.replace with compiled patterns or callables, str.extract with IGNORECASE, or MULTILINE handling pass.

deciding_assertions: test_filter_cond_* (frame and series): df.filter(cond=mask), positional callable or pd.col expression as a mask, na='raise'/True/False; test_filter_positional_bools_select_labels: UserWarning 'A list-like of booleans passed positionally to DataFrame.filter'; TestDataFrameFilter::test_filter: TypeError match 'Must pass a positional argument or one of `items`, `cond`'; messages such as 'cond passed to DataFrame.filter must be a one-dimensional boolean mask'
reason: The issue proposes a `level` argument for DataFrame.filter to select or exclude labels of one MultiIndex level. No hidden test uses `level`; they test a new `cond` boolean-mask argument, a new `na` option, positional-mask warnings, and new error texts. A fix that adds `level` as the issue asks passes none of these tests.

deciding_assertions: test_to_string_na_rep_none_and_na / test_to_html_na_rep_none_and_na [object [1, None]] and [object [1, pd.NaT]]: na_rep='foo' replaces None and NaT, 'None' not in result; test_to_string_na_rep_explicit_nan: explicit na_rep='NaN' gives 4 'NaN' for [None, NA, NaT, nan] while the default shows each as itself, and a datetime column shows 'NaN' with explicit na_rep='NaN'; test_na_rep_none_and_na[category] for to_xml
reason: The issue asks that na_rep replace pd.NA in to_string and to_xml (nullable dtypes and, as a direct variant, pd.NA in object columns and other to_* writers). The narrowest reasonable fix maps pd.NA to na_rep when na_rep differs from the default and makes to_xml fill with a string; it passes the masked/pyarrow/string dtype cases but fails the object None and NaT cases and the explicit-'NaN' test, which needs a sentinel default and covers None, NaT and datetime columns that the issue never mentions.

deciding_assertions: test_complex_ordering_cmp_deprecated (numeric, masked, sparse), test_real_cmp_complex_deprecated, TestNumpyExtensionArray::test_compare_array/test_compare_scalar[complex-*], test_clip_complex_deprecated, test_clip_complex_bound_deprecated: tm.assert_produces_warning(Pandas4Warning, match='deprecated on complex data')
reason: The issue asks that ordering comparisons on complex data raise a TypeError. Every fail-to-pass test instead expects a Pandas4Warning with the message 'deprecated on complex data' and a normal result; a fix that raises TypeError fails all of them. The tests also cover clip, masked and real arrays compared with complex values, and sparse arrays, which the issue does not name.
